reason: Conversation 1 correctly ties the Er03 shutdown to the boil-over liquid on the controls and, once the hob worked again, gave a sensible close: it is fine, wipe up spills promptly, and look at internal components only if it recurs. It makes no unsupported claims about a failed part. Conversation 2 first steers the user toward a cooling fan and vent problem, then ends with a boilerplate water-near-plug electrical warning telling them not to use the hob until an engineer has checked it. That warning contradicts its own 'good news' and does not fit a fully working hob with wiped-dry controls, so it would cause needless alarm and an unnecessary call-out.
